extracted.intended_audience: Foreign and domestic applicants, IP practitioners, technology transfer offices, and attorneys dealing with Thailand IP filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, substantive standards, and procedural steps for obtaining and opposing patents, utility models, trademarks, industrial designs and copyrights in Thailand, including filing language/agent requirements, timelines (publication, opposition, examination), and PCT/Madrid national-phase specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty; Inventive step; Industrial applicability (not required for utility models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory tests for patentability under the Patent Act. Novelty and inventive step must be satisfied for patents; industrial applicability must be shown (explicitly noted as not required for utility models). (Original wording: 'Novelty  Inventive step  Industrial  applicability  (not  for  Utility Models)')

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty and industrial applicability required; inventive step not required for utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models have a shorter term (see durations) and are examined under a lower inventive requirement. (Original wording: 'Utility Models — Novelty; Industrial applicability (not for Utility Models)')

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registrability (novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is required for industrial design protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law requires novelty for designs. The text also notes subject-matter exclusions (designs contrary to public order or morality are non-registrable). (Original wording: 'Industrial Designs — Novelty; ... Designs that are contrary to the public order or morality (art. 58).')

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctiveness; Not in conflict with prior signs; Not generic; Not descriptive; Not contrary to public order/morality; Not contrary to Art. 6ter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prohibitions include flags, state arms, royal seals/monograms/names, national emblems of foreign states, emblems of international organizations, Red Cross, and marks contrary to public order or likely to confuse the public with well-known marks. (Original wording: 'Distinctiveness  Not in conflict with prior signs  Not generic  Not descriptive  Not contrary to public order/morality  Not contrary to Art. 6ter' and long list of prohibited signs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright subject-matter and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works of authorship (literary, dramatic, artistic, musical, audiovisual, cinematographic, sound recording, broadcasting, or any other work in literary, scientific or artistic field). Copyright protection does not extend to ideas, procedures, processes, systems, methods of use or operation, concepts, principles, discoveries, or scientific/mathematical theories. Certain government documents, laws, judicial decisions, official reports are not deemed copyrighted works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists statutory categories of protected works and explicit non-protected categories (Art. 4, 6, 7 references). (Original wording: 'Works  of  authorship ... (art. 6).' and 'Copyright protection shall not extend to ideas or procedures, processes, or systems ... (Art. 6). In addition, the following shall not be deemed copyrighted works (Art. 7): ...')

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright exceptions (permitted uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses allowed only if they do not conflict with normal exploitation and do not unreasonably prejudice the copyright owner (Act. 32): research/study for non-profit; personal/family use; comment/criticism/introduction with acknowledgement; news reporting with acknowledgement; reproduction/adaptation for judicial/administrative proceedings; teacher uses not for profit; reproduction/adaptation/abridgment by teachers for students for non-profit; use in examinations; reasonable citation/quotation with acknowledgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory exceptions specify permitted acts and conditions (acknowledgement, non-profit limits, not prejudicing owner). (Original wording presented in list form under 'Exception to Copyright' and Act.32.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of IP rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents: 20 years; Utility models: 10 years (initial 6 years and two possible renewals of 2 years each); Trademarks: 10 years renewable; Industrial designs: 10 years; Copyright: life of the author plus 50 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durations are statutory terms for each right and include renewal structure for utility models. (Original wording: table entries and statements like '20 years', '10 years for Utility Models (initial 6 years and two possible renewals of 2 years each)', 'Life of author + 50 years'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Thai is the language in which requests must be filed; any document in a foreign language must be accompanied by a Thai translation (Art. 27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to filings and documents submitted to DIP; translations are mandatory for foreign-language materials. (Original wording: 'Thai. If any document ... is in a foreign language, the applicant shall file such document accompanied by translation in Thai. (Art. 27).')

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of agent for foreigners
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant, opposing party, respondent or appellant is not a resident of the country, they shall appoint an agent registered with DIP to act for them in the country (Ministerial Regulations No.21 (B.E.2542)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across patents, designs, trademarks; appointment of a registered Thai agent and power of attorney (when agent appointed) are required for non-residents. (Original wording repeated across sections.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grace period for inventor/other disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: 12 months before the filing date in case of a disclosure: made in consequence of an unlawful act; made by the inventor; made by the inventor displaying the invention at an international exhibition or an official exhibition or an exhibition sponsored or authorized by the government and held in the country (art. 6 and 19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory grace events permit certain disclosed subject-matter to remain patentable if filed within 12 months. (Original wording: '12 months before the filing date, in case of a disclosure: - made in consequence of an unlawful act, - made by the inventor, - made by the inventor displaying the invention at an international exhibition ... (art. 6 and 19).')

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject-matter (statutory exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Naturally occurring microorganisms, their components, animals, plants or extracts from animals or plants; scientific or mathematical rules or theories; computer programs; methods of diagnosis, treatment or cure of human and animal diseases; inventions contrary to public order, morality, health or welfare (Art. 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates classes of inventions excluded from patent protection under Thai law. (Original wording taken from the 'Non-Patentable Subjects' list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination and notification procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: DIP carries out a formality examination; if the application does not comply with requirements, DIP sends notification of rejection asking for amendments; if it complies, DIP sends notification to pay the publication fee within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies at initial filing for patents/designs/trademarks and triggers either amendment requests or progression to publication fee/payment. (Original wording: 'DIP carries out a formality examination. If the application does not comply the requirements under the law, DIP sends notification of rejection to the applicant asking for amendments. If the application complies with the requirements under the law, DIP sends a notification to pay the publication fee within 60 days.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and publication fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DIP publishes the application after payment of the publication fee; notification to pay publication fees is issued after formality compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is a prerequisite for opposition periods and subsequent substantive steps. (Original wording: 'DIP publishes the patent application after payment of the publication fee.' plus flow chart references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition periods and procedures (patents and designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may file oppositions to patent and design applications within 90 days after publication (art. 31; art. 65 for designs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition triggers potential contested proceedings; timelines are statutory (90 days from publication). (Original wording: 'Third parties may file the oppositions to the patent application within 90 days after the publication.' and similar for designs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition period and procedure (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applications are published for 60 days; during that period third parties may file oppositions; if no opposition, the trademark will be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark-specific publication/opposition window is 60 days; oppositions lead to the opposition procedure and potential appeals to the Trademark Board and Courts. (Original wording: 'The trademark application will be published for 60 days. During such period, third parties may file ... oppositions against the trademark application. If there is no opposition ... the trademark will be registered.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination (timing for patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can request substantive examination either within 5 years after the publication or, within 1 year after the final decision has been made in case there is an opposition and an appeal, depending on which period expires last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination is not automatic; the applicant must request it within these statutory time limits. (Original wording: 'Applicants can request for substantive examination either within 5 years after the publication or within 1 year after the final decision has been made in case there is an opposition and an appeal, depending on which period expires last.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination and appeals (patents/designs/trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: DIP carries out substantive examination. The applicant or third parties may file an appeal to the Board of Patents within 60 days after receipt of DIP decision; further appeal to the Court is available within 60 days after receipt of the Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the administrative and judicial appeal windows (60 days) after decisions at each level. (Original wording from filing procedures and flow charts: appeals to Board within 60 days; appeals to Court within 60 days.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry requirements for Thailand
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT international applications designating Thailand should be translated into Thai and enter the national phase within 30 months from the priority date. Filing fees should be paid at this stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional required documents may include name and address of inventor if not in Request, document evidencing change of applicant's name, statement justifying applicant's right to the invention, appointment of a registered agent if applicant not resident, and power of attorney if an agent is appointed. (Original wording: 'PCT international applications designating Thailand should be translated into Thai and enter the national phase within 30 months from the priority date. Filing fees should be paid at this stage.' plus bullet list of special requirements.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-specific documentary requirements (national phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: At national phase submission: name/address of inventor if not in Request; document evidencing change of applicant name; statement justifying applicant's right to the invention; appointment of an agent if not resident; power of attorney if an agent is appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are documents that must accompany PCT national-phase entries to Thailand when applicable. (Original wording: bullet list under 'Other special requirements in this regard are:').

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid system (international trademark) handling by DIP
rubrics_metrics.description: DIP carries out substantive examination within 18 months from receiving the request for extension of protection from WIPO. If the application does not comply, DIP issues a provisional refusal and invites the applicant to respond within 90 days. DIP republishes the international registration for opposition purposes; thereafter the national-level procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the 18‑month examination window, 90‑day response to provisional refusal, and republication for opposition as part of the Madrid route into Thailand. (Original wording from 'Procedures for Obtaining a Trademark in Thailand through the Madrid System' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design and trademark appeals and timelines (procedural flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: For designs and trademarks: formality exam → notification to pay publication fee within 60 days if compliant → publication → opposition window (designs/patents 90 days; trademarks 60 days) → substantive examination → appeals to Board within 60 days → appeals to Court within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow charts in the text set out the sequence and repeated 60/90-day deadlines; applicants must respond or pay fees within the specified windows to progress. (Original wording summarized from multiple 'Procedures' sections and flow charts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited or non-registrable marks and designs (public order/morality and protected symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks and designs contrary to public order or morality are non-registrable. Specific prohibited signs include national flags, state arms/crests, royal seals/monograms/names, emblems of foreign states or international organizations, the Red Cross, and appellations like 'Red Cross' or 'Geneva Cross' unless permission is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions apply to trademark and design filings and may result in refusal; permissions from competent authorities can allow exceptions. (Original wording: long enumerated list under Trademarks and Designs sections.)
